results.problem: Gap between Consistent Guillotine Bound and OPT
results.quote: Theorem 1.2 _For every integer_ \(n'\)_, there is an integer_ \(n\ge n'\)_, and an access sequence X on n keys with_ |_X_|=_n, such that X is a permutation,_ \(\mathsf{OPT}(X)=\Omega(nloglogn)\) _but_ cGB(_X_)=_O(n_logloglog_n)._

results.previous_best: O(loglog n)-approximation in polynomial time (Tango Trees)
results.quote: Theorem 1.3 _There is an offline algorithm for_ Min-Sat_, that, given any integral parameter_ \(D\ge 1\)_, and an access sequence X to n keys of length m, has cost at most_ \(O(D\cdot\mathsf{OPT}(X))\) _and has running time at most_ \(\mathrm{poly}(m)\cdot\mathrm{exp}\left(O\left(n^{1/2^{O(D)}}logn\right)\right)\)_. When D=O_(loglog_n), the algorithm’s running time is polynomial in n and m, and it can be adapted to the online setting, achieving an O_(loglog_n)- competitive ratio._

results.problem: Gap between Second Wilber Bound and Wilber Bound
results.quote: Theorem 4.16 _For every integer_ \(n'\)_, there is an integer_ \(n\ge n'\) _and a point set X that is a permutation with_ |_X_|=_n, such that_ \(\mathsf{WB}^{(2)}(X)\ge\Omega(n\mathrm{loglog}n)\) _but_ \(\mathsf{WB}(X)\le O(n\mathrm{logloglog}n)\).
Lemma 5.3 _For any point set X that is a permutation,_ \(\mathsf{GB}(X)\le 2\mathsf{OPT}(X)\).
